title: Geometric Fixed Parts And Gauss Manin Semisimplicity

items.title: Geometric polarizable Hodge variations on algebraic bases
items.statement: Let $S$ be a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety. A geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation on $S$ consists of a finite-rank rational local system $H$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]), a continuous pure Hodge decomposition of its fibers, or a finite direct sum of pure weights, in the sense of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]], and an algebraic realization on a nonempty Zariski open $U\subseteq S$: there are smooth projective morphisms $f_i:X_i\to U$, degrees $m_i$ and integers $r_i$ such that $H|_U$ is a Hodge direct summand of $$\bigoplus_iR^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i),$$ where $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the Tate structure of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]. A Hodge direct summand means the image of a flat rational idempotent that is a Hodge morphism at every point. A morphism of variations is a flat rational map that is a Hodge morphism at every point. A polarization of a pure object is a flat rational bilinear form with the Hodge positivity property on every fiber; it is not postulated for arbitrary local subsystems: a geometric realization carries one by relative ampleness, and Hodge direct summands inherit it. The closures recorded here under finite sums, tensor products, Hodge direct summands and Tate twists, the exterior-power realizability, the duals via the polarization, and the full monodromy-stable integral lattices are proved by the family construction later on this page; that forward mention is explanatory and is not a prerequisite of the definition.
items.strategy: Definitional. Fixes the objects, morphisms, the direct-summand notion and the polarization convention consumed by the fixed-part and semisimplicity theorems of this page. Source route: the continuous-family and algebraic-family definitions and the closure verification of Deligne II 4.2.1-4.2.5 (continuous Q-Hodge families, polarizations, the conditions (4.2.2.1)-(4.2.2.4), the algebraic category of (4.2.4), and (4.2.5)(i)-(iii)). The only claim-like content is the closure/lattice contract, discharged on this page by the family lemma recorded in `justified_by`; nothing about arbitrary analytic variations is imported, and Schmid's unpublished footnote in Deligne II 4.2.6 is explicitly not used. No choice principle is needed: the definition quantifies over finite data.

references.title: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971) 5-57; SS4.2.1-4.2.5, printed pp. 43-45 (continuous families of Q-Hodge structures, polarizations, the algebraic category)

Claire Voisin, Hodge structures and the topology of algebraic varieties, author-hosted lecture notes (Harvard CMSA revision); SS3.2, printed pp. 38-41 (the local systems attached to smooth projective families)

items.title: Algebraic open inclusions surject on fundamental groups
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $U$ is a nonempty Zariski open subset of a connected smooth complex algebraic variety $S$, then $U$ is path connected and $\pi_1(U,s)\to\pi_1(S,s)$ is surjective for every $s\in U$ ([[def-fundamental-groupoid-of-a-space]]).
items.strategy: Derive analytic charts and irreducibility from smooth regular local rings. Decompose the complement into finitely many smooth pieces including all lower-dimensional components. Smooth based loops on a circle, apply a cutoff-scaled tubular family and parametric transversality, and use a radial parameter homotopy. The tubular supplier uses the proper Whitney embedding in R^(2n+1), giving positive parameter dimension; cutoff zeros lie in constant good neighbourhoods. Treat paths with the same circle construction relative to all junctions.

references.title: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971) 5-57; proof of Theoreme 4.1.1, printed p. 41 (the topological codimension-two step for a Zariski open complement)

Marco Gualtieri, Topology I: Smooth Manifolds, cumulative notes (University of Toronto); Chapter 3 Transversality, printed pp. 25-33 (parametric transversality and the perturbation lemma used for the topological step)

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed in the statement and used to derive AC-$\omega$ for [[thm-parametric-transversality]], [[lem-a-tubular-target-produces-a-submersive-finite-dimensional-perturbation-family]], [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]] and [[thm-relative-whitney-approximation-for-manifold-valued-maps]] through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] (AC => DC => AC-$\omega$); the Jacobian-criterion, classical-scheme and holomorphic-implicit-function suppliers assume AC as well. The stratification, the loop smoothing and the codimension-two computation are otherwise choice-free.

items.title: Geometric Gauss-Manin Hodge variations and integral lattices
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For a smooth projective morphism $f:X\to S$ of smooth quasiprojective complex varieties, $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ is a finite-rank local system ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]), with full monodromy-stable integral lattice obtained from $R^mf_*\mathbb Z$ modulo torsion, and with a continuous pure Hodge decomposition of weight $m$ ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]). A relatively ample line bundle supplies flat Lefschetz operators and a flat rational polarization of this variation. Products, sums, Tate twists, exterior powers and Hodge direct summands have the corresponding geometric realizations and full integral lattices. Pullbacks of algebraic maps between smooth projective fibers preserve rational Hodge structures.
items.strategy: Derive analytic properness from a closed relative projective embedding. Compact horizontal-ODE continuation gives smooth fibre trivializations and inverse-pullback cohomology transport. Supply the integer-valued flasque singular-cochain comparison and the contractible free small-chain quotient, identify higher direct images, and obtain full lattices from finite cellular cochains modulo torsion. Use the bounded inverse of Delta+Pi and constant Betti number for continuous harmonic kernels and Hodge types. The relative ample Chern class yields flat rational Lefschetz polarizations. Rational Kunneth and rational Hodge idempotents give tensor/exterior/summand realizations and intersected lattices; same-degree sums use disjoint unions and different degrees use the finite-sum definition. Extend lattices and forms from the realization open by surjective fundamental groups, density and continuous nondegeneracy.

references.title: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971) 5-57; Theoreme 4.1.1 and SS4.2.1-4.2.5, printed pp. 40-45 (Leray degeneration and the construction of the algebraic category of variations)

Claire Voisin, Hodge structures and the topology of algebraic varieties, author-hosted lecture notes (Harvard CMSA revision); SS3.1-3.2, printed pp. 36-41 (Leray degeneration and the local systems of a smooth projective family)

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used for the compact Kähler supplier [[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]], the elliptic-parametrix supplier [[thm-sobolev-compactness-and-elliptic-estimates-give-fredholm-hodge-decomposition]], the analytic six-operation supplier [[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]], the projective analytification supplier [[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]] and the partition-of-unity theorem [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]. The horizontal-lifting, Künneth and lattice verifications themselves are choice-free.

items.title: Rational descent of a complex monodromy socle
items.statement: Let $A\subseteq\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q}(V)$ be a finite-dimensional rational algebra. The socle ([[def-socle-of-a-module]]) of the $A_{\mathbb C}$-module $V_{\mathbb C}$ is defined over $\mathbb Q$: it is $W\otimes\mathbb C$ for a rational $A$-submodule $W\subseteq V$. If $V\ne0$, then $W\ne0$.
items.strategy: Identify the complex regular-trace radical with the Jacobson radical by positive composition multiplicities. The rational trace matrix descends its kernel. Extend the radical annihilator using finitely many rationally independent coefficients, then identify it with the socle through finite cyclic modules; V need not be finite-dimensional. Nilpotence gives nonvanishing for nonzero V. The full socle is distinct from the minimum-dimensional sum.

references.title: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971) 5-57; SS4.2.6-4.2.7, printed pp. 45-46 (the rational-descent step abbreviated there and supplied here)

items.title: Characteristic-zero scalar extension of geometric semisimplicity
items.statement: Let $S$ be connected and let $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}$ be a finite-rank rational local system ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]). If $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathbb C$ is semisimple, then $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}\otimes k$ is semisimple for every characteristic-zero field $k$ ([[def-semisimple-module]]). In particular this applies to rational Gauss-Manin local systems after complex geometric semisimplicity has been proved. The field $k$ need not embed in $\mathbb C$. Semisimplicity means that every monodromy-invariant subspace has an invariant complement, equivalently that the monodromy module is a finite direct sum of simple modules.
items.strategy: Work separately on each path component. The faithful monodromy algebra over C is semisimple because its nilpotent radical kills every simple summand. Its regular-trace Gram matrix has nonzero rational determinant, hence remains nondegenerate over every characteristic-zero field. Nilpotent trace forces zero radical over that field, and a finite-basis quotient of its semisimple regular modules proves fibre semisimplicity without an embedding into C.

references.title: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971) 5-57; SS4.2.3 and 4.2.6, printed pp. 44-46 (semisimplicity and its coefficient-field independence)

items.title: The fixed part of a geometric Hodge variation
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]) on a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety $S$. For each base point $s$, the monodromy-invariant space $H_s^{\pi_1(S,s)}$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]) is a Hodge substructure of $H_s$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), and parallel transport identifies these spaces as one constant Hodge structure. Equivalently, the Hodge components of every global flat section are global flat sections. For $H=R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ with $f:X\to S$ smooth projective and an SNC smooth projective compactification $\overline X$ of $X$, the image of $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ is exactly the invariant space.
items.strategy: Split relative-dimension parts and shift Rf_*Q by d before applying centered hard Lefschetz; normalize the derived decomposition to give the canonical rational Leray edge a right inverse. Smooth-open functoriality and weight strictness identify the image with the compactification image. The common kernel gives a constant quotient Hodge structure; Hodge components are complex flat sections. Rational Hodge idempotents and surjective open fundamental groups extend the conclusion from a realization open by closed type-membership.

references.title: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971) 5-57; Theoreme 4.1.1(i)-(ii) and Corollaire 4.1.2, printed pp. 40-42 (Leray degeneration and the largest constant subsystem)

Claire Voisin, Hodge structures and the topology of algebraic varieties, author-hosted lecture notes (Harvard CMSA revision); Theorems 3.1-3.3 and Corollaries 3.4-3.5, printed pp. 36-41 (degeneration, the global invariant cycle theorem, and Hodge substructure of the invariant part)

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used through [[lem-smooth-projective-morphisms-give-polarizable-rational-gauss-manin-variations]], the logarithmic-weight supplier [[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]] with its SNC existence lemma, the t-structure splitting and Kähler-identity suppliers, the analytic six-operation supplier and [[lem-algebraic-open-inclusion-surjects-on-fundamental-groups]], all of which assume AC or inherit it. The strictness, weight and flatness arguments themselves are choice-free.

items.title: Semisimplicity of geometric Gauss-Manin local systems
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $f:X\to S$ is smooth projective with $S$ a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety, then every local system $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]) is semisimple over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-semisimple-module]]) and remains semisimple after scalar extension to every characteristic-zero field. More generally the complex local system of every geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation is semisimple. The algebraic realization and geometric integral lattice are essential hypotheses; no claim is made for every polarized analytic variation on a punctured disk.
items.strategy: Descend the full complex socle to Q and intersect its full stable integral lattice, making determinant-square monodromy trivial. Apply fixed part to the rational geometric tensor square, recover torus-image flat lines by projective squaring, contractions and Plucker coordinates. Use orthonormal-frame subsequences and (I-P)MP=0 for each monodromy matrix to prove irreducibility openness, then connectedness of the Hodge torus makes the rational socle Hodge. The precise Weil-operator positivity gives a rational geometric orthogonal complement, so rank induction proves semisimplicity; scalar extension handles every characteristic-zero field.

references.title: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971) 5-57; Theoreme 4.2.6 and Lemme 4.2.7, printed pp. 45-47 (semisimplicity of the monodromy representation and the determinant-line argument)
Claire Voisin, Hodge structures and the topology of algebraic varieties, author-hosted lecture notes (Harvard CMSA revision); SS3.2, printed pp. 38-41 (invariant classes and their Hodge components)

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed and used through [[thm-fixed-part-for-geometric-polarizable-variations-on-smooth-algebraic-bases]], [[lem-smooth-projective-morphisms-give-polarizable-rational-gauss-manin-variations]] and their suppliers; the socle, determinant-line, Grassmannian-compactness and polarization arguments are choice-free.

title: Geometric Fixed Parts And Gauss Manin Semisimplicity Examples

items.title: A cyclic geometric weight-zero monodromy system
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The finite étale morphism $f:\mathbb C^\times\to\mathbb C^\times$, $z\mapsto z^r$, for $r\ge1$, gives a rank-$r$ geometric pure weight-zero local system $R^0f_*\mathbb Q$ ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]], [[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]). Its monodromy cyclically permutes the $r$ sheets and its complexification is a direct sum of one-dimensional root-of-unity characters ([[def-roots-of-unity-in-a-field]]).
items.strategy: The closed projective graph and unit derivative give a finite etale family with r point fibres, type (0,0), full sheet lattice and flat dot-product polarization. Basepoint-fixed radial retraction supplies the positive generator. Forward cohomology transport sends e_a to e_(a+1), while reversed left monodromy sends e_a to e_(a-1); sum zeta^(ja)e_a has eigenvalue zeta^j and inverse Fourier matrix r^-1(zeta^(-ja)). Rank one and fields without roots are included.

references.title: Pierre Deligne, Theorie de Hodge II, Publ. Math. IHES 40 (1971) 5-57; SS4.2.1-4.2.6, printed pp. 43-46 (the weight-zero case of a finite etale family)
Claire Voisin, Hodge structures and the topology of algebraic varieties, author-hosted lecture notes (Harvard CMSA revision); SS3.2, printed p. 38 (local systems of smooth projective families)
